The widening US-ID tech performance gap (5.54% vs 1.01%) signals Jakarta is under-owned, offering catch-up upside as foreign flows rotate into ASEAN tech.
sectors.ai: Buy the ID tech complex into strength; the US AI-semiconductor bid is transmitting to Jakarta via ALAB and SLIS, while local names like IT are re-rating on structural cloud demand. Add on any 3-5% pullback, overweight semis and data-center proxies, and trim laggards without direct AI exposure.

sectors.name: Renewables & Climate-Tech
themes: Indonesia's nickel downstreaming and EV battery integration create a durable cost-advantage moat for domestic climate-tech names, independent of global rate cycles.

Electrification of Indonesia's two-wheeler and bus fleets is a multi-year structural driver, supported by government subsidies and local content rules that favor domestic assemblers.
sectors.ai: Buy the Indonesia electrification complex on VKTR/TOBA strength; US solar (SEDG, ENPH, FSLR) is a tactical bounce, not a trend shift. sectors.name: Consumer & FMCG

Government subsidies and food-security policies, including rice and cooking-oil price controls, keep input costs stable for FMCG producers, supporting margin resilience despite global commodity swings
sectors.ai: Buy selective small-cap FMCG names riding the IDX momentum wave, but avoid chasing the +10% movers (COIN, BTEK, SMLE) as they are likely speculative rotations with thin liquidity. Favor ADES and AGAR for their water/consumer staples exposure, which offers defensive volume growth amid Indonesia's stable domestic demand. Trim positions into any further upside, as the sector's aggregate +0.81% signals consolidation, not a breakout.

Trim TBMS and BR on valuation, hold MIRA for toll-road traffic recovery. Watch for policy catalysts from the new cabinet's infrastructure budget; position defensively in utilities and data-center power plays.

sectors.name: Logistics
themes: Indonesia's coal and nickel export volumes remain the structural demand anchor for heavy-haul logistics firms like TRUK and RMKE, with port congestion and barge rates sustaining pricing power.
Digital freight aggregation and last-mile consolidation are compressing margins for asset-light players (SOCI, BLOG), favoring integrated asset owners with terminal and fleet control.
US freight forwarders (EXPD, CHRW) are pricing in a global restocking cycle, which historically transmits to Indonesian shipping rates within 2-3 quarters, supporting forward earnings revisions.
sectors.ai: Buy logistics selectively on the IDX: TRUK's +25% confirms port-to-mine volume leverage, while SOCI and RMKE ride coal/commodity haulage momentum. US names (EXPD, CHRW) signal global freight pricing firmness, but ID exposure is the cleaner alpha. Accumulate TRUK on pullbacks, add RMKE for commodity-linked upside; avoid TAXI (structural taxi irrelevance).
